introduction: On this Sunday, Isaiah promises that God will comfort his people as a mother comforts her child. In the Gospel, Jesus sends out seventy-two disciples in pairs, telling them that the harvest is great but the laborers are few. They return with joy, and Jesus tells them to rejoice that their names are written in heaven. Paul boasts only in the cross of Christ. Let us go out as laborers in the Lord's harvest.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the harvest is abundant, but the laborers are few. Let us ask the Lord of the harvest to send laborers.
intentions: For the Church: that the Lord of the harvest may send many laborers to proclaim his Kingdom. Let us pray to the Lord.
For vocations to the priesthood, the diaconate, religious life and lay ministry: that many may answer the Lord's call. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who bring peace to homes and communities: that their peace may rest on those they meet. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who need comfort: that God may comfort them as a mother comforts her child. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may rejoice that our names are written in heaven. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord of the harvest, you send your disciples out to prepare the way for your Son. Send laborers into your harvest, and make us messengers of your peace. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The laborers are few
reflection.body:
Isaiah gives us one of the most tender images of God in the Bible. Speaking to a people returning from exile, God says, "As one whom his mother comforts, so I will comfort you." Jerusalem is pictured as a mother nursing her children, and God's peace flows "like a river."

In the Gospel, Jesus sends out seventy-two disciples, not only the Twelve. Luke wants us to see that the mission is for many. Jesus sends them "two by two ahead of him into every city and place where he was about to come." They prepare the way for him.

Before they go, he gives them something to pray for: "The harvest is indeed plentiful, but the laborers are few. Pray therefore to the Lord of the harvest, that he may send out laborers into his harvest." Then he sends them out "as lambs among wolves," carrying almost nothing. Their first word in every house is to be peace: "Peace be to this house." They are to heal the sick and announce, "God's Kingdom has come near to you."

The disciples return full of joy: even the demons obeyed them. Jesus shares their joy but points them to something greater: "don't rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven." Success in ministry is a gift, but our deepest joy is that God knows and loves us.

Paul tells the Galatians what he boasts in: "far be it from me to boast except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ." The mission is not about our achievements but about Christ.

This week, pray each day for laborers for the harvest, for priests, religious and lay people who share the faith. And be a laborer yourself: bring a word of peace to someone, and let them see that God's Kingdom is near.
